description: What this plugin believes Claude Code can do, and how each belief was established. One file so that a platform refresh is a diff against a checked model rather than a re-reading of every document.
why: This repository has been wrong in both directions. It emitted permissionDecision "escalate" for ten versions, a value the CLI does not accept, so every escalate-tier rule silently allowed the command it described. It also documented `effort` as unsupported on plugin agents when the CLI validates it.

Both mistakes were cheap to make because each belief lived in prose, in a different file, established at a different time, with no record of how it was checked. A capability the code depends on should say how it was verified and when.

It also recorded PermissionRequest as unavailable on the strength of a probe that only covered the two modes which short-circuit before the hook runs. An absence has to be checked the way a presence is, or it becomes the most confident kind of wrong entry.

evidence_levels.contract: Declared in the CLI's own schema. The strongest evidence short of running it.
evidence_levels.empirical: Observed on the wire in this environment.
evidence_levels.documented: Stated in the published documentation and not independently confirmed here.
evidence_levels.absent: Checked for and not found. An absence that can be relied on.

hook.SubagentStart.additionalContext.note: Declared as `hookEventName:Ht("SubagentStart"),additionalContext:O().optional()` and confirmed on the wire. Injected into the subagent's message list only when the spawn is not isolatedContext; an isolated spawn silently receives no briefing, which is the exact failure inject_context.py exists to prevent. SubagentStart hooks are skipped entirely for delegated-observation subagents.

hook.SubagentStop.last_assistant_message.note: Carries agent_id, agent_type, last_assistant_message and agent_transcript_path.

hook.TaskCompleted.can_block.note: Carries task_id, task_subject, optional task_description, teammate_name and team_name. No hookSpecificOutput variant exists for this event, so it cannot inject or rewrite; it is in the CLI's blocking set, so exit 2 blocks the completion. A gate, not an orchestrator.

hook.TaskCreated.carries_dependencies.note: Payload is task_id, task_subject, task_description?, teammate_name?, team_name?. team_name is marked @deprecated in the CLI's own schema ('Sessions have a single implicit team; this carries the session-derived team name and will be removed in a future release'). No blocks, blockedBy or metadata reaches the hook: the native engine keeps those edges internally -- its task-delete path strips a deleted id out of every other task's blocks/blockedBy -- but does not send them. teammate_name is the only assignee signal and is a display name, not a registry role. This is why the task graph is the plugin's own artifact rather than a mirror of Claude Code's list.

hook.PermissionRequest.fires_headless.note: Corrected at 2.1.241. It is NOT gated on interactivity: executePermissionRequestHooks is the only tool-lifecycle emitter with no registration guard, and the headless branch runs the hooks before returning its 'permission prompts are not available' deny. The earlier probe found nothing because dontAsk denies before that branch and auto short-circuits ahead of it -- an absence of firing under two modes was read as an absence of the capability. Nothing here depends on it.

permission_decision.values.note: allow, deny, ask, defer. A value outside this set is discarded and the tool call PROCEEDS -- visibly the first time, then silently, because the error is latched once per (event, command). That is why the escalate bug survived ten versions. defer is print-mode only and solo-only, so ask is the only usable escalation on the wire.

agent_frontmatter.effort.note: Validated against low, medium, high, xhigh, max or an integer.

agent_frontmatter.ignored_for_plugins.note: permissionMode, hooks and mcpServers are warned about and discarded on a plugin agent. Setting one would be configuration that does nothing.

agent_teams.note: Requires CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS, and spawning a teammate requires an interactive session: the documentation states that under -p, including SDK sessions, "Claude doesn't spawn teammates, and a subagent that Claude names runs as an ordinary subagent even with agent teams enabled". Teammates are not worktree-isolated, so work given to a team must be partitioned by file. Nothing in the lifecycle may depend on teams.
agent_teams.corrected: v0.22 recorded teams as no longer interactive-only, on the strength of print-mode teammate lifecycle strings in the binary and a --teammate-mode in-process flag. That was an over-read: a print-mode session can BE a teammate or manage one, which is not evidence that a print-mode lead can SPAWN one. The earlier reading was right and this file was wrong for four versions. Same error as the PermissionRequest entry, mirrored: there an absence was inferred from a probe that could not have seen it, here a presence was inferred from strings that did not say it.
agent_teams.cannot_be_detected: No environment variable distinguishes an interactive session from -p: CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT is "cli" in both, verified. So resolve_execution.py cannot check interactivity, and the degradation is covered the other way instead -- a team that becomes an ordinary subagent is recorded in execution.actual, and the divergence from execution.resolved is written to the work item history.

worktree_isolation.note: isolation: worktree on a spawn or in agent frontmatter. worktree.baseRef defaults to fresh, so an isolated worker does not see unpushed local commits.

native_task_list.note: TaskCreate/TaskGet/TaskUpdate/TaskList with real blocks and blockedBy edges (confirmed). On-disk layout not re-confirmed at 2.1.241. Gated behind CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS on some models. Execution state on one machine, which is why it is not the system of record here.

dynamic_workflows.note: A workflows/ directory at the plugin root, JavaScript only, runs under -p. Gated by the enableWorkflows / disableWorkflows settings, so an organization can switch it off. Not shipped: the lifecycle is declarative on purpose. Used for review fan-out over this repository, which is what it suits.

lsp_servers.note: A .lsp.json at the plugin root. Deliberately not shipped: extensionToLanguage is not variable-expanded and extension claims are global across plugins, so a placeholder would outrank a project's real server.

host.fcntl_flock.note: POSIX only. scripts/lib/workitem.py serialises concurrent task claims with fcntl.flock and falls through when the import fails, so on a host without it claims are NOT serialised and two agents can be handed one task. The lease, the graph and every predicate still work; only the concurrency guarantee is absent.
host.fcntl_flock.if_absent: Run one agent at a time, or set concurrency limits to 1 in policies/concurrency-policy.json. Windows is untested.

hook.TeammateIdle.can_block.note: Declared as hook_event_name:Ht("TeammateIdle"),teammate_name:O(),team_name:O() -- team_name is marked deprecated -- and TeammateIdle is in the CLI's blocking set, so exit 2 keeps the teammate working. It carries NO agent_id, which is what a task lease is keyed by, so a teammate can only be matched to a lease by name. hooks/scripts/teammate_idle.py blocks only on an unambiguous single match and is silent otherwise; the name-to-lease correlation is unverified end to end here because it needs a live team.

hook.Worktree.lifecycle.note: WorktreeCreate carries `name`; WorktreeRemove carries `worktree_path`. Neither carries a task or an agent, so the events are recorded as evidence that isolation happened during a change and deliberately not bound to a task -- correlating by timing would look like knowledge and be a guess.

hook.SubagentStart.identifies_the_spawn_.note: The payload is agent_id and agent_type only: no teammate marker, no isolation flag. So execution.actual can be claimed as `subagent` only where agent teams are off; where the flag is on, a spawn could be either and the task records actual_undetermined instead of guessing.

agent_frontmatter.documented_and_unused.note: The subagent frontmatter supports more than this plugin uses: disallowedTools, maxTurns, memory, background, initialPrompt, and an Agent(type) form in `tools` that restricts which subagents an agent may spawn. All are listed as working normally for plugin agents. `disallowedTools`, `maxTurns`, `memory`, `background` and `initialPrompt` are present in the 2.1.241 binary; the frontmatter path for Agent(type) was not confirmed there, only the internal allowedAgentTypes field.
agent_frontmatter.documented_and_unused.why_unused: The spawn hierarchy is enforced by hooks/scripts/guard_spawn.py, which works and is tested. Replacing a verified enforcement with an unverified one is a regression even when the unverified one is more mechanical. Adopting Agent(type) as a second layer needs the frontmatter path confirmed first.

hook.TaskCreated.can_block.note: Exit 2 does not warn: the CLI's own help text says 'show stderr to model and prevent task creation', and executeTaskCreatedHooks collects blockingError, deletes the just-created task and strips its id from every other task's edges before throwing. TaskCreated is in the same blocking set as Stop, TeammateIdle and TaskCompleted. There is no hookSpecificOutput variant, so it cannot inject or rewrite -- the binding it establishes has to be written to the graph and read back later.
hook.TaskCreated.can_block.re_verified: 2026-08-28 against 2.1.250 and again against 2.1.251, by reading the binary. The upgrade renamed the variable holding the blocking set from `aen` to `_in`, which failed the drift belief on a capability that was entirely intact -- the belief now matches the array literal rather than the name holding it.

agent.memory.project_scope.note: `memory: project` in an agent's frontmatter gives it a persistent store at <project>/.claude/agent-memory/<agent-type>/, as MEMORY.md plus one file per entry. The scope enum is user | project | local, resolved in the binary to the home directory, the project's .claude, and a local-only path respectively. The CLI's own guidance text says project scope is 'shared with your team via version control' and local scope is 'not checked into version control', so project scope is designed to be committed and reviewed.
agent.memory.project_scope.verified: 2026-08-28 against 2.1.250, live: a real `claude -p` session delegated to an agent declaring memory: project, and .claude/agent-memory/<agent>/MEMORY.md plus an entry file appeared in the project tree. Not gated behind a flag.

agent.memory.elaborates_what_it_is_told.note: Memory does not only record. Given the bare fact 'the retention window is 30 days', the probe agent wrote back an invented justification ('likely driven by compliance standards, regulatory frameworks, or internal data governance policies') and promoted the fact to a rule it would enforce ('Flag any architectural decisions or cleanup operations that might violate this window'). Nobody said either. This is why memory is never organizational authority here: left alone it manufactures a `why` and an imperative, and next session it applies both as though they were policy.
agent.memory.elaborates_what_it_is_told.used_by: the memory instructions in the five roles that hold it, which forbid both

agent_frontmatter.skills_apply_to_a_team.note: Claude Code applies an agent definition's `skills:` frontmatter when the role runs as a subagent, and not when the same definition runs as a teammate. So a role documented as holding a capability arrives without it the moment a stage resolves to `team` -- silently, because nothing errors and the role simply reasons without the skill. skills/team-patterns/SKILL.md therefore tells every spawn prompt to invoke the needed skills explicitly.
agent_frontmatter.skills_apply_to_a_team.used_by: skills/team-patterns/SKILL.md; check_team_stages_carry_their_skills in scripts/validate_plugin.py, which requires every team-execution stage to declare the skills its teammates cannot inherit
agent_frontmatter.skills_apply_to_a_team.evidence_limit: Documented, not confirmed against the binary: no teammate/skills string was found in 2.1.251 by inspection, and confirming it properly needs a live team, which has never run here. It is recorded as load-bearing anyway, because a check now depends on it and the failure mode -- a teammate reasoning without a capability it is documented to hold -- is silent.

refresh: When the tested_against version moves, re-verify every capability marked load_bearing before anything else. Those are the ones whose failure is silent.

when_the_docs_and_the_binary_disagree.rule: The installed binary wins, and the disagreement is recorded here rather than resolved silently. Documentation describes intent across versions; the binary is what runs on this machine today.
when_the_docs_and_the_binary_disagree.why_this_section_exists: Following the published docs on the first row below would reintroduce, exactly, the bug this repository shipped for ten versions: every escalate-tier rule silently allowing the command it describes. A capability model that only reads documentation is not safer than one that reads nothing.

disagreements.subject: permissionDecision values
disagreements.binary_says: allow, deny, ask, defer. The string "escalate" does not appear in the 2.1.241 binary at all, and the runtime throws "Unknown hook permissionDecision type ... Valid types are: allow, deny, ask, defer".
disagreements.consequence: A guard following the documentation emits a value the CLI discards, and the tool call proceeds. This is the highest-stakes row here.
disagreements.this_plugin: hooks/lib/hooklib.py maps its internal `escalate` to the wire value `ask`. Correct against the binary.

disagreements.subject: TaskCompleted / TaskCreated payload
disagreements.consequence: A hook reading task_title reads nothing.

disagreements.subject: TeammateIdle payload
disagreements.binary_says: teammate_name and a deprecated team_name. There is no teammate_id.
disagreements.consequence: A teammate cannot be correlated to a task lease by id, because no id is sent. Only a name is available.
disagreements.this_plugin: teammate_idle.py matches by name and acts only on an unambiguous single match.

disagreements.subject: WorktreeCreate payload
disagreements.consequence: A hook reading worktree_path on create reads nothing.
disagreements.this_plugin: record_worktree.py reads both and records whichever arrives.

disagreements.subject: SubagentStart output
disagreements.binary_says: hookEventName:Ht("SubagentStart"),additionalContext:O().optional() -- it is in the output schema, and injection was confirmed on the wire.
disagreements.consequence: Following the docs, nobody would build context injection at all. This plugin's whole briefing path depends on it.
disagreements.this_plugin: inject_context.py returns additionalContext and it arrives.

disagreements.subject: SubagentStart payload
disagreements.consequence: Nothing here depends on it; recorded so a future version adding it is noticed rather than assumed.

first_live_run.why_it_matters: Until this, every hook had been tested by feeding hand-written JSON to a Python script. 547 tests and 28 faults validated the plugin against itself; none of them proved that Claude Code would ever call any of it. That is a different claim and it had never been checked.
first_live_run.how: A throwaway project registered the hooks by absolute path in its own .claude/settings.json -- project scope only, nothing installed globally -- and real `claude -p` sessions were run in it.
verified_live: SubagentStart fires, claims exactly one task, resolves its execution, and the briefing reaches the subagent: the agent reported the work item id, the intent verbatim and its definition of done, none of which were in the prompt it was given.
SubagentStop attributes the result to that task by agent_id, and releases the lease.
A spawn whose agent_type owns no task is recorded as subagent_stopped_unattributed rather than guessed at -- observed with a real agent_id.
execution_diverged fired on a real divergence: the stage declared `inline` and the work actually ran as a subagent. The evidence names the real agent id.
guard_bash escalates a protected-branch push in a live session: the refusal text reached the model, the command never ran, and the audit recorded decision=escalate rules=GIT-00.
The SessionStart self-test runs and its Tier-0 deny is recorded.

The Golden Project certification path: `scripts/certify.py --live` against golden/, with this plugin's hooks and agents registered project-scope by absolute path. Kept as golden/certification-run.json.
A live session's write outside the role's scope was refused by guard_write and the refusal recorded in the audit log.

execution.actual disagreed with execution.resolved on a real task -- T-001 declared inline, resolved inline, actual subagent -- and the divergence was recorded from SubagentStart evidence. Until this, actual and resolved had never been observed to differ, which is consistent with actual being copied rather than observed.
An agent briefed only by SubagentStart reported its work item id and the intent verbatim, neither of which was in its prompt.

An agent held a task whose gates did not close, declined to mark it done, declined to dispatch the next one, and the task's state stayed queued. The organization's refusal to self-accept was observed rather than asserted.
still_never_run: Agent teams. Requires an interactive session and the experimental flag.
Worktree isolation, and therefore the briefing_required path where an isolated spawn receives no injected context.

Both task gates. TaskCompleted and TaskCreated need the native task tools, which no session here has used. Their payload shape and their place in the blocking set are read from the binary by scripts/check_platform_drift.py; that neither has ever been called by a real session is a different claim and still untested.

Any complete work item. Real agents have now driven one stage of one work item (GOLD-FEAT-001, T-001) under certification; no change has been driven from intake to acceptance by real agents, and certify.py reports certified: false because of it.
